subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures what the city is doing, continuously and densely.
parts: inductive loops and cameras at junctions
GPS traces from vehicles and phones

subsystems.name: Communications and data fabric
subsystems.role: moves those measurements to where they can be used, in a common format.

subsystems.name: Digital twin
subsystems.role: a live model of the city's roads, pipes, wires and buildings that can be simulated forward.

subsystems.name: Prediction and control layer
subsystems.role: forecasts demand and decides what to change.

subsystems.name: Actuation layer
subsystems.role: the physical handles the system can turn.
parts: grid switches, batteries and flexible loads

subsystems.name: Governance and resilience
subsystems.role: keeps a city-wide controller safe, lawful and recoverable.

buildSteps.title: Instrument one domain
buildSteps.detail: Start with a single system — usually traffic signals or the distribution grid — and fit it with sensors, meters and remote control.

buildSteps.title: Standardise the data
buildSteps.detail: Agree schemas and interfaces so that data from different departments and vendors can be joined without bespoke glue code.

buildSteps.title: Build the digital twin
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a live model of assets and flows, calibrated against measured behaviour until its predictions match reality.

buildSteps.title: Forecast
buildSteps.detail: Train models to predict demand minutes to days ahead — traffic volumes, electricity load, water draw, waste generation.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop on one domain
buildSteps.detail: Let the model adjust signals or shift flexible load automatically, with tight limits and a human kill switch.

buildSteps.title: Couple domains
buildSteps.detail: Link the models so an action in one domain is checked against the others — for example, shifting bus routes when a substation is constrained.

buildSteps.title: Add autonomous optimisation
buildSteps.detail: Replace hand-tuned rules with learned controllers that continuously trade off travel time, energy cost, emissions and equity — validated in simulation before live use.

buildSteps.title: Harden and operate
buildSteps.detail: Red-team the system, define degraded modes for network or sensor failure, and keep an auditable record of every automatic decision.

prerequisites.why: without continuous measurement there is nothing to control.

prerequisites.tech: Low-latency urban connectivity and edge compute
prerequisites.why: control decisions must arrive faster than the traffic or load changes.
several cities run twins, but few are real-time or span more than one domain.
traffic and load forecasts work separately; coupled forecasts degrade quickly.
the 'city-level AGI' element does not exist; today's controllers are narrow and domain-specific.

prerequisites.tech: Cybersecurity and privacy frameworks for city data
prerequisites.why: a system that can turn every signal and switch is a high-value target.

pathway.milestone: domain-specific optimisation already in service: adaptive traffic signal control, grid demand response, leak detection in water networks
pathway.unlocks: measurable savings without any city-wide intelligence.

pathway.milestone: multi-domain digital twins that share a common state model
pathway.unlocks: city planners can test interventions before building them.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop control across two or three coupled domains with strict safety envelopes and human oversight
pathway.unlocks: coordination benefits, such as charging electric fleets when the grid is cleanest.

pathway.milestone: learned city-wide control, if general-purpose AI with verifiable safety ever matures
pathway.unlocks: the claimed autonomous urban optimisation — speculative, and gated on AI reliability and public consent, not on sensors.
